All rights reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.</copyright-statement></permissions><self-uri xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" content-type=\\\\\\\"pmc-pdf\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"jamadermatol-e250982.pdf\\\\\\\"/><self-uri xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" content-type=\\\\\\\"pdf-version\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"jamadermatol-e250982.pdf\\\\\\\">jamadermatol-e250982.pdf</self-uri><self-uri xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" content-type=\\\\\\\"silverchair\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"https://jamanetwork.com/journals/archderm/fullarticle/10.1001/jamadermatol.2025.0982\\\\\\\"/><abstract abstract-type=\\\\\\\"key-points\\\\\\\"><title>Key Points</title><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-1\\\\\\\"><title>Question</title><p>What are the efficacy and adverse events of ivarmacitinib treatment in adolescents and adults with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis?</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-2\\\\\\\"><title>Findings</title><p>This phase 3 randomized clinical trial of 336 patients (age ≥12 years) found that significantly more patients in the 4- or 8-mg ivarmacitinib groups achieved an Investigator Global Assessment score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-grade improvement from baseline and an Eczema Area and Severity Index score improvement of at least 75% compared to the placebo group. Serious treatment-emergent adverse events occurred at low and similar rates across all groups.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-3\\\\\\\"><title>Meaning</title><p>These findings show that ivarmacitinib is an effective treatment with a favorable risk-benefit profile for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis in adults and adolescents.</p></sec></abstract><abstract><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-4\\\\\\\"><title>Importance</title><p>Ivarmacitinib, a selective oral Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy for treating adults with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD) in a phase 2 trial.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-5\\\\\\\"><title>Objective</title><p>To evaluate the efficacy and adverse events of ivarmacitinib in adolescents and adults with moderate to severe AD.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-6\\\\\\\"><title>Design, Setting, and Participants</title><p>This multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized clinical trial included patients aged 12 to 75 years with moderate to severe AD. Patients were enrolled from 53 sites in Canada and China from April 2021 to April 2022. Data were analyzed from July 11 to September 27, 2023.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-7\\\\\\\"><title>Interventions</title><p>Patients were randomized (1:1:1) to receive once-daily 4- or 8-mg ivarmacitinib or placebo for 16 weeks.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-8\\\\\\\"><title>Main Outcomes and Measures</title><p>Co-primary end points were the proportions of patients achieving an Investigator Global Assessment (IGA) score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with at least a 2-grade improvement from baseline and an Eczema Area and Severity Index score improvement of 75% (EASI-75) at week 16.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-9\\\\\\\"><title>Results</title><p>Of 336 randomized patients (mean [SD] age, 31.1 [15.4] years; 213 [63.4%] male; 286 [85.1%] Asian), 113 received 4-mg ivarmacitinib, 112 received 8-mg ivarmacitinib, and 111 received placebo. At week 16, significantly more patients in the 4-mg ivarmacitinib group (41 of 113 [36.3%]; 95% CI, 27.5%-45.9%; <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">P</italic> &lt; .001) and the 8-mg ivarmacitinib group (47 of 112 [42.0%]; 95% CI, 32.7%-51.7%; <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">P</italic> &lt; .001) achieved an IGA score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-grade improvement compared to the placebo group (10 of 111 [9.0%]; 95% CI, 4.4%-15.9%). EASI-75 responses were also significantly higher in the ivarmacitinib groups: 61 patients (54.0%; 95% CI, 44.4%-63.4%; <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">P</italic> &lt; .001) in the 4-mg group, and 74 (66.1%; 95% CI, 56.5%-74.8%; <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">P</italic> &lt; .001) in 8-mg group compared to 24 patients (21.6%; 95% CI, 14.4%-30.4%) in the placebo group. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported by 78 patients (69.0%) in the 4-mg group, 74 (66.1%) in the 8-mg group, and 72 (64.9%) in the placebo group. Serious treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 3 patients (2.7%) in the 4-mg group, 2 (1.8%) in the 8-mg group, and 3 (2.7%) in the placebo group.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-10\\\\\\\"><title>Conclusions and Relevance</title><p>This phase 3 randomized clinical trial determined that once-daily ivarmacitinib demonstrated significant efficacy and a favorable risk-benefit profile for treating moderate to severe AD in adults and adolescents. These results support the potential of ivarmacitinib as a new therapeutic option.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"ab-doi250014-11\\\\\\\"><title>Trial Registration</title><p>ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: <ext-link xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04875169\\\\\\\" ext-link-type=\\\\\\\"uri\\\\\\\">NCT04875169</ext-link></p></sec></abstract><abstract abstract-type=\\\\\\\"teaser\\\\\\\" specific-use=\\\\\\\"electronic\\\\\\\"><p>This phase 3 randomized clinical trial evaluates the efficacy and adverse effects of ivarmacitinib for treatment of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis in adults and adolescents.</p></abstract><custom-meta-group><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-status-qastatus</meta-name><meta-value>0</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-status-live</meta-name><meta-value>yes</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-status-embargo</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-status-released</meta-name><meta-value>yes</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-open-access</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-olf</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-manuscript</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-legally-suppressed</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-has-pdf</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-has-supplement</meta-name><meta-value>yes</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-pdf-only</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-suppress-copyright</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-is-real-version</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-is-scanned-article</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-preprint</meta-name><meta-value>no</meta-value></custom-meta><custom-meta><meta-name>pmc-prop-in-epmc</meta-name><meta-value>yes</meta-value></custom-meta></custom-meta-group></article-meta></front></article></pmc-articleset>\\\",\\nfixtures/positive/a-atopic-dermatitis/research-content.json:252846: ValidYN=\\\\\\\"Y\\\\\\\">10.1001/jamadermatol.2025.5295</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"IMPORTANCE\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">ICP-332 is a tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor currently under investigation for the treatment of atopic dermatitis (AD).</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"OBJECTIVE\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">To evaluate the safety and efficacy of ICP-332 for moderate to severe AD.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">This double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 randomized clinical trial was conducted between February 6 and November 7, 2023, across 19 centers in China. Individuals aged 18 to 75 years who had diagnosis of AD for 1 year or longer and a history of contraindication or inadequate response to topical therapies were included.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"INTERVENTION\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive ICP-332 at 80 mg or 120 mg, or placebo orally once daily for 4 weeks. Study participants and personnel were blinded to group assignment.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">The primary outcome was safety. The key efficacy outcome was the percentage change from baseline in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) at week 4. Other outcomes included percentages of patients achieving EASI-75 (a &#x2265;75% improvement in EASI) and Validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis score of clear (0) or almost clear (1) with 2 or more points improvement.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"RESULTS\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">This study included 75 patients (mean [SD] age, 37.3 [18.0] years in the ICP-332 groups and 44.5 [17.4] years in the placebo group; 21 women [28%] and 54 men [72%]). Among the 74 patients included in the safety set, 17 of 25 (68%) in the placebo group, 19 of 25 (76%) in the 80-mg ICP-332 group, and 18 of 24 (75%) in the 120-mg ICP-332 group experienced treatment-emergent adverse events, with all events being mild or moderate. The most common adverse event was decreased blood fibrinogen (1 of 25 [4%] in the placebo group, 6 of 25 [44%] in the 80-mg ICP-332 group, and 5 of 24 [21%] in the 120-mg ICP-332 group). Percentage reductions in EASI at week 4 were -78.2% (95% CI, -89.8% to -66.6%) in the 80-mg ICP-332 group, -72.5% (95% CI, -84.3% to -60.7%) in the 120-mg ICP-332 group, and -16.7% (95% CI, -28.7% to -4.6%) for those receiving placebo. Mean differences vs placebo for percentage reductions from baseline at week 4 in EASI were -61.6% (95% CI, -78.4% to -44.7%; P&#x2009;&lt;&#x2009;.001) and -55.8% (95% CI, -72.8% to -38.9%; P&#x2009;&lt;&#x2009;.001) for 80-mg ICP-332 and 120-mg ICP-332, respectively. There was a statistically significant higher EASI-75 response rate with both ICP-332 doses (64.0% for each; difference vs placebo, 56.0%; 95% CI, 34.4%-77.6%; P&#x2009;&lt;&#x2009;.001) than with placebo and a greater percentage of Validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis score of 0 or 1 and improvement of 2 or more points at week 4 in the 80-mg ICP-332 group vs placebo (36.0%; difference vs placebo, 32.0%; 95% CI, 11.7%-52.3%; P&#x2009;=&#x2009;.005).</AbstractText><AbstractText Label=\\\\\\\"CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE\\\\\\\" NlmCategory=\\\\\\\"UNASSIGNED\\\\\\\">In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, ICP-332 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and encouraging efficacy, supporting further development for To view a copy of this licence, visit <ext-link xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" ext-link-type=\\\\\\\"uri\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/\\\\\\\">http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/</ext-link>.</license-p></license></permissions><self-uri xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" content-type=\\\\\\\"pmc-pdf\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"13555_2025_Article_1368.pdf\\\\\\\"/><abstract id=\\\\\\\"Abs1\\\\\\\"><sec><title>Introduction</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par1\\\\\\\">Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease. 611, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively targets the interleukin (IL)-4 receptor alpha, thereby inhibiting the signaling of both interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13. This phase 2 study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD.</p></sec><sec><title>Methods</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par2\\\\\\\">This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study was conducted between October 2022 and September 2023. Eligible patients with moderate-to-severe AD were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 611 at a dose of either 300 mg (loading dose of 600 mg) every 2 weeks (Group A) or 300 mg (loading dose of 600 mg) every 4 weeks (Group B), or placebo every 2 weeks for 16 weeks, followed by an 8-week follow-up period. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 75% reduction in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) score at week 16. The safety and pharmacodynamics were also assessed.</p></sec><sec><title>Results</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par3\\\\\\\">After 16 weeks of treatment, 60.0% of patients in Group A and 48.8% in Group B achieved EASI-75, both significantly higher than the placebo group (15.6%, <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">p</italic> &lt; 0.01). Additionally, 611 at both doses significantly improved the Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) scores, peak pruritus numerical rating scale (NRS), and other efficacy endpoints. Patients receiving 611 demonstrated significant reductions in serum thymus activation-regulated chemokine (TARC) and total serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels. The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) was similar across all dosage groups. The most common 611-related TEAE is upper respiratory tract infections. No new safety concerns were identified.</p></sec><sec><title>Conclusion</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par4\\\\\\\">611 demonstrated a high efficacy and a favorable safety profile in patients with moderate-to-severe AD.</p></sec><sec><title>Trial Registration</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par5\\\\\\\">ClinicalTrials.gov, <ext-link xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" ext-link-type=\\\\\\\"pmc:clinical-trial\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"NCT05544591\\\\\\\">NCT05544591</ext-link>.</p></sec><sec><title>Supplementary Information</title><p>The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s13555-025-01368-4.</p></sec></abstract><kwd-group xml:lang=\\\\\\\"en\\\\\\\"><title>Keywords</title><kwd>Atopic dermatitis</kwd><kwd>Chinese 2025</meta-value></custom-meta></custom-meta-group></article-meta></front><body><sec id=\\\\\\\"d33e470\\\\\\\"><title>Key Summary Points</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par6\\\\\\\">\\\\n<table-wrap id=\\\\\\\"Taba\\\\\\\" position=\\\\\\\"float\\\\\\\" orientation=\\\\\\\"portrait\\\\\\\"><table frame=\\\\\\\"hsides\\\\\\\" rules=\\\\\\\"groups\\\\\\\"><tbody><tr><td align=\\\\\\\"left\\\\\\\" colspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\" rowspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\">Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with significant disease burden and limited treatment options for moderate-to-severe cases. An unmet need remains for novel biologic treatments that effectively target the underlying pathophysiology of AD while maintaining a favorable safety profile.</td></tr><tr><td align=\\\\\\\"left\\\\\\\" colspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\" rowspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\">This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-4 receptor alpha (IL-4Rα), in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD.</td></tr><tr><td align=\\\\\\\"left\\\\\\\" colspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\" rowspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\">Treatment with 611 demonstrated significant improvement in disease severity as measured by the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75), Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) 0/1 response, and reductions in pruritus and inflammatory biomarkers compared to placebo. The incidence of adverse events, including treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), was comparable across treatment and placebo groups, indicating a favorable safety profile.</td></tr><tr><td align=\\\\\\\"left\\\\\\\" colspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\" rowspan=\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\">This study supports the potential of 611 as an effective therapeutic option for moderate-to-severe AD and highlights the need for further investigation in diverse populations to confirm its long-term efficacy and safety.</td></tr></tbody></table></table-wrap>\\\\n</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec1\\\\\\\"><title>Introduction</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par7\\\\\\\">Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense pruritus. In Chinese adults, the 1-year prevalence of adult AD was 6.13%, and the point prevalence of AD was 2.42% [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR1\\\\\\\">1</xref>]. The point prevalence of AD based on clinical diagnosis by dermatologists was 12.94% overall, ranging from 9.00% to 24.69% between metropolises for preschool children in China [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR2\\\\\\\">2</xref>–<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR4\\\\\\\">4</xref>]. The pathogenesis of AD involves a complex interplay between environmental and genetic factors, resulting in immune dysregulation [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR5\\\\\\\">5</xref>]. Major immune abnormalities include allergen presentation, T-helper 2 cell (Th2)-driven responses, impaired regulatory T cells, excessive immunoglobulin E (IgE) production, and increased eosinophils [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR6\\\\\\\">6</xref>–<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR10\\\\\\\">10</xref>]. Type 2 inflammation, primarily mediated by interleukin (IL)−4 and IL-13, is thought to play a central role in AD pathogenesis [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR11\\\\\\\">11</xref>]. Elevated IL-4 and IL-13 levels are associated with AD severity, facilitating IgE production, macrophage activation, eosinophil recruitment, and pruritus through IL-4Rα signaling in neurons [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR12\\\\\\\">12</xref>].</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par8\\\\\\\">Dupilumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody, targets the IL-4/IL-13 signaling to inhibit a major source of inflammation associated with AD. Since its approval in 2020 by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), dupilumab has been used to treat moderate-to-severe AD in China. 611 is a recombinant humanized immunoglobulin-G4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody that inhibits IL-4 and IL-13 signaling. Preclinical and phase 1 clinical studies have validated the safety and tolerability of subcutaneous administration of 611 in healthy subjects. This phase 2 study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in patients with moderate-to-severe AD.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec2\\\\\\\"><title>Methods</title><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec3\\\\\\\"><title>Study Design, Patients, and Treatment</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par9\\\\\\\">This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, <ext-link xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" ext-link-type=\\\\\\\"pmc:clinical-trial\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"NCT05544591\\\\\\\">NCT05544591</ext-link>) was conducted across 23 sites in China. This study adhered to the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki for medical research involving human subjects and was conducted in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. Before the study commenced, the clinical trial protocol, case report forms, informed consent forms, and other related documents were approved by the Peking University People’s Hospital Ethics Committee (approval number: 2022PHC022-001). All patients provided written informed consent for participation in the study. The study duration for each participant was 28 weeks, including a screening period of up to 4 weeks, a 16-week treatment period, and an 8-week follow-up period. Patients aged 18–75 years with moderate-to-severe AD were enrolled. Inclusion criteria included a baseline Investigator’s Global Assessment (IGA) score of ≥ 3, Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score of ≥ 16, ≥ 10% body surface area (BSA) of AD involvement, and a weekly average peak pruritus numerical rating scale (NRS) score of ≥ 4. Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are outlined in Supplementary Table S1. After screening, eligible subjects were stratified by IGA scores (3 or 4) and randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to the following groups: Group A (611 300 mg every 2 weeks with a 600 mg loading dose), Group B (611 300 mg every 4 weeks with a 600 mg loading dose), or placebo. All participants used emollients at least 7 days before randomization and continued this regimen throughout the study.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec4\\\\\\\"><title>Endpoints and Assessments</title><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec5\\\\\\\"><title>Efficacy Assessments</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par10\\\\\\\">The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving at least a 75% reduction in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) score at week 16. Secondary endpoints included the proportion of participants achieving EASI-50, EASI-90, IGA score of 0 or 1 (0/1) with ≥ 2 point reduction, and ≥ 4 points or ≥ 3 points in the weekly average peak pruritus NRS score from baseline to week 16. The Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) and Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure (POEM) were also evaluated. (A list of all efficacy endpoints is provided in Supplementary Table S2).</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec6\\\\\\\"><title>Safety Assessments</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par11\\\\\\\">Safety assessment included treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), vital signs, physical examinations, electrocardiograms (ECGs), and clinical laboratory test results.</p></sec></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec7\\\\\\\"><title>Biological Markers</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par12\\\\\\\">Pharmacodynamic markers included TARC, total serum IgE, peripheral blood eosinophil count (EOS), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH).</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec8\\\\\\\"><title>Statistical Analysis</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par13\\\\\\\">The sample size calculation was based on the primary endpoint (the percentage of subjects achieving an EASI-75 response at week 16). Assuming EASI-75 response rates of 49.2% for 611 and 11.5% for the placebo group at week 16, a sample size of 90 subjects with a randomization ratio of 1:1:1 was required to achieve a stated power of 80% to show superiority of 611 over placebo at a significance level of <italic toggle=\\\\\\\"yes\\\\\\\">α</italic> = 0.05 (two-sided) accounting for a 10% dropout rate. The calculation is based on Fisher’s exact test for the binomial distribution using PASS 2019 software.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par14\\\\\\\">The primary analysis and binary endpoints were conducted in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis set, which included all randomized subjects, using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test adjusted for stratification factors [baseline IGA score (3 or 4)] to compare the proportions of subjects between treatment groups. Intercurrent events, including the use of rescue therapy, administration of prohibited medications affecting the interpretation, or discontinuation of treatment due to lack of efficacy, were classified as non-responders from that time. Missing data were imputed using the non-responder imputation (NRI).</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par15\\\\\\\">For continuous efficacy endpoints (e.g., a change from baseline in EASI score), an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model was employed to estimate the least square means (LSM) of changes from baseline to week 16 while controlling for baseline covariates and stratification factors. The intercurrent events, similar to the primary endpoint, were considered missing and imputed using the baseline observation carried forward (BOCF) from that time. Missing data were imputed using multiple imputation (MI), and the statistical inferences obtained from all imputed data were combined using Rubin’s rule. Safety analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics in the safety population, including all randomized subjects who received investigational drugs by treatment group.</p></sec></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec9\\\\\\\"><title>Results</title><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec10\\\\\\\"><title>Baseline Characteristics</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par16\\\\\\\">A total of 120 subjects were screened, and 30, 31, and 32 subjects were assigned to Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively (Fig. <xref rid=\\\\\\\"Fig1\\\\\\\" ref-type=\\\\\\\"fig\\\\\\\">1</xref>). Nine patients withdrew from the study predominantly because of lack of efficacy (1 patient each in Groups A and B, and 7 patients in the placebo group).<fig id=\\\\\\\"Fig1\\\\\\\" position=\\\\\\\"float\\\\\\\" orientation=\\\\\\\"portrait\\\\\\\"><label>Fig. 1</label><caption><p>Patient disposition. Flowchart showing the enrollment, randomization, and follow-up of patients in the phase II trial. A total of 120 patients were screened, with 93 randomized into three groups: Group A (611 300 mg every 2 weeks), Group B (611 300 mg every 4 weeks), and placebo. Nine patients discontinued the study because of lack of efficacy, predominantly in the placebo group</p></caption><graphic xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" id=\\\\\\\"MO1\\\\\\\" position=\\\\\\\"float\\\\\\\" orientation=\\\\\\\"portrait\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"13555_2025_1368_Fig1_HTML.jpg\\\\\\\"/></fig></p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par17\\\\\\\">Demographics and baseline clinical characteristics, including gender, age, height, weight, and BMI, were well balanced across the treatment groups (Table <xref rid=\\\\\\\"Tab1\\\\\\\" ref-type=\\\\\\\"table\\\\\\\">1</xref>). The proportion of subjects with an IGA score of 3 was 56.7%, 58.1%, and 56.3% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. The mean baseline EASI scores were 28.7, 26.2, and 28.6 in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. The other subject was found to have left lung cancer during the follow-up period post-treatment. It was regarded as unrelated to 611. In Group B, one subject experienced two Grade 3 TEAEs: the first event was pneumonia occurring during the treatment period, which improved after treatment and was regarded as unrelated to 611; the slightly higher in both 611 treatment groups (26.7% and 16.1%) compared to the placebo group (12.5%), and the severity was all Grade 1 or 2. Upper respiratory tract infections were the most common treatment-related TEAEs in both 611 treatment groups, with 6.7% in group A and 3.2% in group B.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par22\\\\\\\">No significant abnormalities were detected in physical examinations, vital signs, ECGs, or laboratory tests across the three groups.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec13\\\\\\\"><title>Change in Biological Markers</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par23\\\\\\\">At week 16, the median percent reductions from baseline in TARC levels were 60.8%, 58.8%, and 28.9% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. Treatment with 611 resulted in a rapid and sustained reduction in TARC levels. By week 24, approximately 10–12 weeks after the last dose, TARC levels gradually returned to baseline values.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par24\\\\\\\">At week 16, the median percent reductions in total serum IgE levels were 49.7%, 36.6%, and 0% in Group A, Group B, and the placebo group, respectively. The total serum IgE levels showed a gradual decrease with treatment. No significant differences in EOS and LDH were detected between the 611 treatment and placebo groups.</p></sec></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec14\\\\\\\"><title>Discussion</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par25\\\\\\\">This study demonstrated that 611 was effective in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. The EASI-75, EASI-90, and IGA 0/1 in the two treatment groups were superior over the placebo group. The regimen of 600 mg + 300 mg Q2W showed a more robust and rapid response in achieving IGA 0/1, whereas the regimen of 600 mg + 300 mg Q4W exhibited comparable improvement at week 16. The 300 mg Q2W was selected as the preferred regimen during the core treatment period, whereas the 300 mg Q4W was adopted during the maintenance period in the Phase 3 clinical trial (<ext-link xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" ext-link-type=\\\\\\\"pmc:clinical-trial\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"NCT06173284\\\\\\\">NCT06173284</ext-link>).</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par26\\\\\\\">Subjects receiving treatment with 611 showed notable improvements in itch symptoms as early as week 2, with 10% and 16.1% of subjects in Groups A and B achieving an NRS score ≥ 4, which was similar to those of the dupilumab Q2W group (9% ~ 11% [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR13\\\\\\\">13</xref>]). By week 4, 23.3% and 12.9% of subjects in Groups A and B achieved an NRS score ≥ 4 (dupilumab Q2W: 16%–23% [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR13\\\\\\\">13</xref>]). By week 16, 46.7% and 45.2% of subjects in Groups A and B, respectively, achieved an NRS score ≥ 4 (dupilumab Q2W: 36% ~ 41% [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR13\\\\\\\">13</xref>]). Overall, receiving 611 every other week demonstrated similar efficacy to dupilumab in relieving patients’ symptoms. The incidence of rescue therapy was significantly lower in 611 treatment groups compared to the placebo group. The proportions of subjects who had used rescue therapy at least once were 16.7% (5/30), 12.9% (4/31), and 31.3% (10/32) in Group A, B, and placebo, respectively.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par27\\\\\\\">Common adverse reactions associated with dupilumab in clinical studies for atopic dermatitis include injection site reactions (including erythema, edema, pruritus, pain, and inflammation), conjunctivitis, allergic conjunctivitis, arthralgia, oral herpes, and eosinophilia. In this study, only 1.6% of subjects treated with 611 experienced injection site reactions and injection site erythema related to the experimental drug (vs. dupilumab SOLO 1 and SOLO 2—injection site reactions: 8%–19%), and 1.6% of subjects treated with 611 experienced allergic conjunctivitis (vs. dupilumab SOLO 1 and SOLO 2—conjunctivitis: 3%–5%); all of the above were significantly lower than those found in SOLO 1 and SOLO 2. The lower incidence of conjunctivitis observed with 611 compared to dupilumab may be attributed to differences in molecular structure, binding affinity, or immune modulation beyond IL-4Rα inhibition. While both 611 and dupilumab target IL-4Rα, subtle variations in pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity may contribute to differences in adverse event profiles. Further investigations, including comparative clinical and mechanistic studies, are necessary to elucidate the underlying reasons for these observed differences.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par28\\\\\\\">TARC and IgE are biological markers indicative of type 2 inflammation [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR14\\\\\\\">14</xref>]. 611 demonstrated a significant effect on the decrease of TARC and IgE levels. This finding further supports the specific mechanism of action of 611 in inhibiting IL-4 and IL-13 signaling pathways. Changes in EOS and LDH were minimal and showed a weak correlation with clinical improvements.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par29\\\\\\\">AD exhibits genetic and phenotypic variations across different populations. Several studies have reported that East Asian patients with AD, including those in China, often present with unique clinical features, such as a higher prevalence of lichenification, the highest levels of TH17/TH22 activation among all ethnic groups, higher serum IgE levels compared to European populations, and a higher frequency of filaggrin gene mutations than African populations, which are closely associated with impaired skin barrier function [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR15\\\\\\\">15</xref>]. These genetic and phenotypic differences may contribute to variations in AD pathogenesis and treatment responses. Furthermore, studies have shown that Asian patients with AD exhibit more pronounced type 2 and type 17 inflammatory responses, which may influence therapeutic efficacy [<xref ref-type=\\\\\\\"bibr\\\\\\\" rid=\\\\\\\"CR16\\\\\\\">16</xref>]. Therefore, although the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese patients align with global findings on IL-4Rα inhibitors, further investigations in diverse populations are necessary to establish its broader applicability.</p><p id=\\\\\\\"Par30\\\\\\\">While this study provides valuable insights into the efficacy and safety of 611 in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD, several limitations should be considered. First, this study was conducted exclusively in a Chinese adult population, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to other ethnic groups. Further research is needed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 611 in a more diverse global population, including pediatric patients. Second, the relatively short follow-up period (16 weeks of treatment plus an 8-week follow-up period) restricts the ability to assess the long-term efficacy and safety of 611, particularly regarding potential adverse events that may emerge with prolonged use. Two ongoing Phase 3 studies with a 52-week treatment period are currently being conducted to further evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of 611. Finally, while the study assessed key clinical endpoints such as EASI-75, IGA 0/1, and pruritus reduction, further investigation is required to determine the broader applicability of 611 in clinical practice.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec15\\\\\\\"><title>Conclusion</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par31\\\\\\\">611 showed good efficacy and favorable safety profiles in Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe AD, achieving significant improvements across multiple efficacy endpoints compared to the placebo group. The results of this Phase 2 study underscore the potential of 611 as an IL-4Rα antibody for treating AD in adult patients, offering a promising new therapeutic option for those with moderate-to-severe AD.</p></sec><sec id=\\\\\\\"Sec16\\\\\\\" sec-type=\\\\\\\"supplementary-material\\\\\\\"><title>Supplementary Information</title><p>Below is the link to the electronic supplementary material.<supplementary-material content-type=\\\\\\\"local-data\\\\\\\" id=\\\\\\\"MOESM1\\\\\\\" position=\\\\\\\"float\\\\\\\" orientation=\\\\\\\"portrait\\\\\\\"><media xmlns:xlink=\\\\\\\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\\\\\\\" xlink:href=\\\\\\\"13555_2025_1368_MOESM1_ESM.pdf\\\\\\\" position=\\\\\\\"float\\\\\\\" orientation=\\\\\\\"portrait\\\\\\\"><caption><p>Supplementary file1 (PDF 248 KB)</p></caption></media></supplementary-material></p></sec></body><back><fn-group><fn><p><bold>Prior Presentation:</bold> Parts of these data were previously presented as an e-Poster (British Journal of Dermatology, Volume 191, Issue Supplement_1, July 2024, Pages i54–i55) at the 104th British Association of Dermatologists Annual Meeting (BAD 104th), held in Manchester, UK, from July 2–4, 2024.</p></fn></fn-group><ack><title>Acknowledgements</title><p>The authors thank all the investigators and patients who participated in this trial.</p><sec id=\\\\\\\"FPar4\\\\\\\"><title>Authorship</title><p id=\\\\\\\"Par32\\\\\\\">All named authors meet the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors criteria for authorship for this article.
